newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Sampo invests T$100mln in Taiwan retail strategy.
newsitem.headline: Sampo invests T$100mln in Taiwan retail strategy.

text.p: Consumer electronics maker Sampo Corp on Monday said it was buying up to 40 percent of local high-tech distributor Runcomp International to deepen its drive into the island's retail electronics market.
"We have signed a contract with Runcomp International Corp to purchase a stake of between 35 and 40 percent worth over T$100 million," Sampo chairman Felix Chen told reporters.

Chen said the move aimed to pave the way for Sampo, one of Taiwan's top consumers electronic makers, to enter its "three C" market, which he defined at a news conference as consumer electronics, computers and communications.
Chen said Sampo planned to transform its own 80 Taiwan sales outlets into "three C" retail supply centres in 1997, with Runcomp acting as a source of popular hardware.
Runcomp, which had T$990 million in 1996 sales, is a Taiwan agent for Seagate, Novell, Hewlett-Packard and other international computer brands.
Sampo, itself a popular Taiwan brand name, had pretax profit of T$704 million on 1996 sales of T$18.5 billion. Its 1997 pretax profit target is T$850 million on sales of T$20 billion.
